name: sdc-rs
summary: Rust client library for DRED — channel subscription, message posting, channel management, Ed25519 signing, and reliable reconnection
activities: Subscribe to DRED channels via NDJSON streaming with per-channel async receivers
Post messages and manage channels (list/create/encrypted-create) via REST
Rotate connections gracefully when subscribed channel set changes
responsibilities: Deduplicate incoming messages via two-generation rotating HashSet keyed on ocid
Detect dead connections via heartbeat watchdog (3x server interval)
Suppress sender's own echo by pre-registering ocid in dedup before posting
Sign channel names with Ed25519 for encrypted channel ownership proofs
Provide per-listener child CancellationTokens so individual subscriptions can be stopped without affecting others

name: DredClient (TS parent)
summary: TS DredClient — the parent architecture's client component that sdc-rs reimplements a subset of
surrogateReason: sdc-rs is a Rust reimplementation of a pragmatic subset of this TS component's functionality

name: DredServer
summary: DRED server node — the remote endpoint that sdc-rs connects to
surrogateReason: sdc-rs connects to DredServer for all HTTP and streaming operations

name: DredSubscription
summary: Managed subscription handle — owns listener task, per-channel receivers, supports connection rotation via update_channels()
activities: Own listener lifecycle and per-channel mpsc senders/receivers
Rotate connections on channel-set changes (new connects before old cancels)
responsibilities: Preserve existing receivers across rotation for channels present in both old and new sets
Cancel old listener only after new listener's connected signal fires
Clean up failed rotation attempts via CancelGuard drop safety

name: DredListener
summary: Internal streaming listener — connects to /channels/listen, parses NDJSON, deduplicates, routes to per-channel senders
activities: Maintain persistent NDJSON connection with heartbeat monitoring and reconnection
Parse messages and route to per-channel mpsc senders after dedup
responsibilities: Monitor heartbeat interval and declare connection dead after 3x timeout
Fire connected_signal oneshot on first parsed message (used by DredSubscription for rotation sequencing)
Reconnect with exponential backoff (reset when connection was alive longer than backoff_max)

name: Deduplicator
summary: Two-generation rotating HashSet for ocid-based message deduplication — shared across reconnections via Arc, poison-safe
activities: Track seen ocids across a 30-60s window using current/previous generation rotation
responsibilities: Bound memory by rotating generations every 30s (configurable)
Survive mutex poisoning via PoisonError::into_inner recovery
Support concurrent access from multiple listeners and the post_message pre-dedup path

name: Identity
summary: Ed25519 signing identity — wraps dryoc crypto_sign_detached, wire-compatible with TS StringNacl
activities: Sign strings and verify detached Ed25519 signatures with base64-encoded wire format
responsibilities: Match TS client StringNacl wire format (64-byte detached sig over UTF-8 bytes base64-encoded)
Support keypair persistence via base64 export/import

name: DredMessage
definition: pub struct DredMessage { mid, channel, msg_type, nbh, msg, ocid: Option<String>, extra: Map<String, Value> }
discussion: Serde struct for NDJSON wire format — known fields typed, extras captured via #[serde(flatten)]

name: DredError
definition: pub enum DredError { Transport(reqwest::Error), ServerStatus(StatusCode), Protocol(String), StreamEnded, Cancelled }
discussion: Enumerated error type (Send+Sync+'static) with source() chaining for Transport variant

name: Subscribe & Stream
description: Client subscribes to channels, server streams NDJSON messages through a persistent connection

name: Post Message
description: Client posts a message to a channel with echo suppression via pre-dedup

name: Connection Rotation
description: Subscription rotates connection when channel set changes — new connects before old cancels

name: Message Delivery Pipeline
description: Server → NDJSON stream → line parse → heartbeat filter → dedup check → per-channel routing → mpsc receiver
trigger: Server flushes an NDJSON line on the chunked HTTP response
postconditions: Message delivered to exactly one consumer (or dropped if no receiver for that channel)
